Senses.PreferredTarget: a young girl with forked hair-knots, her hair white as silk
SearchAliases: a young girl with forked hair-knots, her hair white as silk
Senses.Note: 丫角 indicates a girl's forked or horn-like hair arrangement, not literal horns. Preserve the whole young-and-old image rather than resolving its contradiction. No lamp is retained.

Occurrences.Kwic: 人來相問山何境，徹底從頭舉似伊，急著眼，莫遲疑，丫角女子白頭絲。咦。投子指菴前石投子布山漫天網，雪峰走入伊圈套
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J10/J10nA158.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Miyun. Touzi Datong's answer words are retained verbatim in Miyun Yuanwu's verse within Miyun's own record.

Occurrences.Kwic: 示眾示眾丫角女子白頭絲。報儞諸方作者知。借問住山何境界。春風𩖼𩖼春鳥喧喧。翠峯不能助發。心印却是他傳。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (T/T47/T47n1996.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Mingjue, whose own stupa inscription inside the work gives the master's taboo name as Chongxian. Xuedou Chongxian owns the admonition deployment: addressing the assembly he opens with the horned-bun maiden's white-headed silk, tells the makers of all quarters they are hereby informed, lends the question of what realm a mountain-dwelling has, and closes that the spring wind and spring birds cannot help it forth — the mind-seal alone was transmitted by him.

Occurrences.Kwic: 投子因僧問：和尚住此山有何境界？師曰：丫角女子白頭絲。丫角女子白頭絲，猛燄堆中雪片飛，一等住山誰可擬？閒雲流水不同歸。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X69/X69n1351.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Baiyun Shouduan, his own verse on the raised case. Baiyun Shouduan owns the versifying deployment: after the case of the monk asking Touzi what realm his mountain has and Touzi answering with the horned-bun maiden's white-headed silk, Baiyun's own verse takes the line as its opening — snowflakes flying in a raging blaze of flame — asks what ordinary mountain-dweller could match it, and grants that idle clouds and flowing waters do not return together.

Occurrences.Kwic: 上堂云。窮萬化之淵源。得一真之住處。體空而了了。不涉根門。照盡而綿綿。全超塵想。直得光境俱斷。心法兩忘。卓爾獨存。廓然圓湛。生滅去來。不我遷變。便能應緣無礙。靜照亡功。所以僧問投子。如何是和尚安樂處。子云。丫角女子白頭絲。師云。諸禪德。當明有暗。當暗有明。鬧浩浩中靜悄悄。靜悄悄中明歷歷。還委悉麼。良久云。行到水窮處。坐看雲起時。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (T/T48/T48n2001.xml). Extensive Record of Chan Master Hongzhi. Hongzhi Zhengjue owns the commenting deployment: in hall he traces the source of the myriad transformations to the dwelling place of the one truth — essence empty yet lucid, freed from the sense-gates, shining spent yet continuous, wholly past the dust-thoughts — then raises that a monk asked Touzi what his place of ease was and Touzi answered with the maiden line, and comments to the worthies of Chan: within light there is dark, within dark there is light, quiet within the noisy clamor, distinct within the quiet, sealing it after a long silence with walking to where the water ends and sitting to watch the clouds rise.

Senses.Explanation: Touzi Datong answers the mountain-scenery question with a girl's forked hair-knots and white hair joined in one impossible image. Touzi Datong uses the expression through case commentary and verse. Touzi Datong's answer words are retained verbatim in Miyun Yuanwu's verse of his own record.

Senses.PreferredTarget: ask where Chang'an is from inside Hanyuan Hall
AlternateTargets: look for the capital while standing in its palace
SearchAliases: seek outside what is already present
ask for an entrance while already inside
Senses.Note: The palace is already in Chang'an, so the location mismatch supplies the idiom's rebuke of an unnecessary outward search.

Senses.Explanation: To “ask where Chang'an is from inside Hanyuan Hall” is to seek an entrance or destination while already standing at its center. Fushi Tongxian uses it as a reply to a question about host and guest; Huizhou Hao says looking for the Way apart from words and appearances resembles this mistake; Dahui Zonggao applies it to searching for a starting point outside one's own inquiry. The palace-capital mismatch therefore rebukes an unnecessary outward search.

AlternateTargets: to spray another person with blood
Senses.Note: Three independent records retain the same reflexive consequence, not merely the two-character act of spitting.

Occurrences.Kwic: 各各眾生前贊此功德。便使此一一微塵身，代一切微塵地獄諸苦有大歡喜矣。宅有兒爾庚，甫八歲，似有種性者，甚惟達觀老師及藏兄所憐，今以身師事達觀老師，而以兒事藏兄，助緣隨化父子共之云。弟子傅光宅薰沐和南謹書瞿汝稷書刻大藏願文我佛菩薩視眾生沉沒苦流，不啻身受其苦，欲拯之覺岸，乃竭其慈力，因病授藥，巧譬曲喻，慇懃反覆，誘掖眾生，故有是一大藏。稷自髫歲則喜讀其言，今年已四十，顧根器凡狹，菩提涅槃尚在遙遠。然歷諸患苦，患苦恬謐，歷諸險阻，險阻坦夷，仰荷慈力，深遠難量。旋視九界眾生，其患苦險阻如稷者、過於稷者，殆不可勝計。念是而不贊佛弘化，則真斷佛種性之忍人。慈值密藏師兄欲梓方冊全藏以廣流通，欣然契心，遂尾諸淨侶，長跽佛前，而說誓曰：「願畢我形壽，力荷此法藏，苟可效我力，靡所不自竭。念昔佛菩薩，以此法藏故，剝皮以為紙，析骨以為筆，書寫此經卷，積如須彌山。今此真丹國，陟釐瑩於玉，無事以我皮，充此法藏用，使我皮可用，剝所不敢辭。域有蒙氏筆，無事析我骨，使我骨可用，析所不敢辭。我今雖食貧，檀貲當勉具，歷仕及歸農，隨緣力為辦。不直此一生，願盡未來際，常以此法藏，普度諸眾生。」那羅延窟學人瞿汝稷盥沐槃談書唐文獻書刻大藏願文文獻溷，風塵久，且根器鈍劣，無能窺大道。頃歲從達觀大師密藏禪師稍聞緒論，始知佛恩最大，欲報無繇。中夜思之，可勝慚赧。

Occurrences.Kwic: 以公滅私，於是宗風大振。未幾年，訥公厭閴寂，郡守至，自陳客情，太守惻然目端，端笑唯唯而已。明日登座曰：昔日大法眼禪師有偈曰：難難難是遣情難，情盡圓明一顆寒。方便遣情猶不是，更除方便太無端。大眾且道情作麼生遣？喝一喝，下座，包腰而去。一眾大驚，遮留之不可，叢林至今敬畏之。南禪師住廬山歸宗，火一夕而燼，大眾譁譟動山谷，而黃龍安坐如平時。桂林僧洪準欲掖之而走，顧見叱之，準曰：和尚縱厭世間，慈明法道何所賴耶？因徐整衣起，而火已及座榻矣。坐是入獄，郡吏發其私忿，考掠百至，絕口不言，唯不食而已。兩月而後得釋，鬚髮不剪，皮骨僅存。真點胸迎於中塗，見之不自知，泣下曰：師兄何至是也？黃龍叱曰：者俗漢！真不覺拜之。蓋其不動如山類如此。曹山躭章禪師初辭洞山悟本，本曰：吾在雲巖先師處親印寶鏡三昧，事窮的要，今付受汝。汝善護持，無令斷絕，遇真法器，方可傳委。直須秘密，不得影露，恐屬流布，喪滅吾宗。夫末法時代，人多乾慧，若要辨認向去之人真偽，有三種滲漏，當機直須具眼：一、見滲漏者，機不離位，墮在毒海；二、情滲漏者，智常向背，見處偏枯；三、語滲漏者，體妙失宗，機昧終始，濁智流轉。於此三種，子宜知之。又綱要三偈，初敲倡俱行，曰：金針雙鎻備，狹路隱全該，寶印當空妙，重重錦縫開。其次金鎻玄路，曰：交牙明中暗，功齊轉覺難，力窮尋進退，金鎻網鞔鞔。

Senses.Explanation: Whose house's tune do you sing? challenges a teacher to show which lineage his public performance expresses. The musical image asks about a recognizable house style, while the commonly paired follow-up—'whose lineage style do you inherit?'—asks for succession. Linji answers with his three questions and three blows under Huangbo; Baoyue and Yuelu answer in the idiom of their own records.

Senses.Note: The phrase is a narrative turn marker. The surrounding biography or section identifies the master whose question follows, while the headword-bearing words themselves belong to the recorder's narration.

Senses.PreferredTarget: A nun is, after all, a woman
SearchAliases: a nun is, after all, a woman
Senses.Note: In an older case, a monk says he awakened to the fact that a nun is a woman. Later masters use the same plain words in new turns. Feiyin closes a verse with them; Baichi answers a nun who asks for the abiding mark; Chaozong uses them after comparing the teachings of earlier masters. Yushan asks whether even this answer goes too far, while Tianyin gives it to a visitor asking for an unseparated phrase. The line brings the question back to what is already in front of the hearer.

Senses.Explanation: The lion appears through cubs, roars, and full-force capture in the stored Chan encounters. Chan records repeatedly deploy the animal in lineage and speech vocabulary: a capable successor is a 'lion cub' and forceful proclamation is a 'lion's roar.' The Blue Cliff Record pairs an outstanding, keen fellow with a lion cub; Zhaozhou is called a true lion cub, well able to roar. A recorded old adept says that a lion uses its complete strength for both rabbit and elephant, then names that strength the strength that does not deceive. Another inherited formula contrasts proclamation with attainment, calling teaching with something obtained a jackal's cry and teaching without something obtained a lion's roar. These are explicit corpus uses; the entry assigns no hidden animal symbolism.

Senses.Explanation: Patriarch Simha is the named twenty-fourth lineage figure: records narrate his beheading and list his place between named successors. As a personal name, Siṃha denotes the Twenty-fourth Indian Patriarch, not the animal lion. The Patriarchs' Hall Collection heads his record 'The Twenty-fourth Patriarch, Venerable Siṃha,' identifies him as a man of central India, and records his entrusting the eye of the true teaching onward. A transmission roster independently places Venerable Siṃha between the Twenty-third and Twenty-fifth Patriarchs. Qianyan's record later raises the inherited case in which the king of Kashmir cuts off Venerable Siṃha's head. A person numbered in the lineage and beheaded by a king is a different referent from the lion used in lion cub and lion's roar. The Chan corpus invokes this pre-Chinese figure through his lineage place and death case; that Zen use defines the person sense here.

Senses.Explanation: Linji uses the lion's single roar and the jackal's split skull as a verdict on the force of a great teacher before turning against timid teachers and claims of a path to cultivate. The Record of Linji and two later recensions transmit Linji Yixuan's same address. He says a great teacher dares to criticize buddhas, patriarchs, and established teaching, and concludes: when the lion roars once, the jackal's skull splits.

Senses.Explanation: The lion’s roar is explicitly defined against the jackal’s cry as teaching without something gained, and later records demand, test, or appraise that roar in public exchange. In the Chan record it names forceful speech or teaching and is repeatedly opposed to the cry of a jackal. One record supplies an explicit definition: ‘teaching with something gained is the jackal's cry; teaching with nothing gained is called the lion's roar’ (說法有所得，斯則野干鳴；說法無所得，是名師子吼). The phrase is not merely an appraisal applied by compilers: Baozi Guangyun tells his interlocutor to ‘try making a lion's roar,’ and monks claim it, and it becomes a public-interview challenge. Guishan says that Shishuang's speaking of Chan is ‘like a lion's roar, frightening the foxes, wolves, and jackals to death.’ In another exchange an unnamed monastic asks what happens on meeting a lion's roar; Shoushan Xingnian answers ‘let the jackal cry as it likes,’ after which the unnamed monastic shouts. Thus an animal sound is bent into a name, test, and verdict for speech in the teaching encounter; the texts themselves establish the lion/jackal contrast without requiring an imported symbolic reading.

Senses.Explanation: The lion bites the person is one half of a contrast: the lion turns on the thrower while the hound chases the clod. Case verses and comments pair it with the hunting hound pursuing a lump, distinguishing attention to the acting person from pursuit of the object thrown. Dazhu Huihai uses the same comparison when answering why someone who follows written formulations does not see. Later raised cases apply the pair as a verdict on who follows the immediate object and who confronts its source.

Senses.Note: A lion bites the person, while the famed Hanlu hound runs after a thrown clod. Fushi offers the contrast as his own replacement answer; Guxue uses it to answer a question about different lineages; Hansong and Mixing apply it to new case comments and questions. The full pair is the teaching unit because the two pursuits define each other.

Senses.Explanation: The phrase compares something to a lion advancing vigorously and also occurs in the name of an absorption. Senses.Note: One retained letter explicitly gives this as the name of an absorption; that title-like use is not collapsed into the animal simile.

Occurrences.Kwic: 僧自恣，萬人叢裡奪高標，到頭恰似小兒戲。雪峯輥三箇木毬，仰山推出枕子，蛇頭揩痒，虎頷編須，不有師子爪牙，便見橫尸萬里。是你諸人九十日內渴飲飢餐、早眠晏起，既云識果知因，且免破規越矩。卓拄杖，云：水東流，日西去，三更五更唱巴歌，無端驚起梵王睡。

Occurrences.Kwic: 箭射。師云：好語要且無來處，有人辨得出，與你一兩金。下座。上堂。盡大地無一粟米大，十有九箇刺頭入膠盆。有般瞎漢只管說，照用同時，人境俱奪。盖為鑪鞴之所，鈍鐵尤多；良醫之門，病者愈甚。報恩更作死馬醫，未免撞入漆桶隊裏。復舉：金峰和尚一日因僧問訊，乃把住云：輒不得道我有一則因緣舉似你。僧作聽勢，峰與一掌，僧云：為什麼打某甲？峰云：我要者話行。師云：者僧雖深入虎穴，要且未具師子爪牙。金峰雖有師子爪牙，爭柰有頭無尾？汝等諸人還知報恩著力處麼？一點水墨，兩處成龍。上堂，僧問：呈橈舞棹則不問，且道婆婆手中兒子甚處得來？巖頭扣船舷三下，未審意旨如何？師云：焦甎打著連底凍。進云：當時若問，和尚如何對佗？師云：一棒打殺。進云：者老和尚大似買帽相頭去也。師云：你向什麼處見巖頭？僧云：劄。師云：杜撰禪和。進云：婆生七子，六箇不遇知音，只者一箇也不消得，便擲向水

Senses.Explanation: Lion claws and fangs form an animal image of fierce Chan capacity. Liaoan says that without them corpses would lie for ten thousand li; Zhean praises a predecessor with the same image, and a useful lamp lists them among the four requisites of a teacher. Yingan uses the image to assess an old case, while Yuechuang applies it to an addressees ability to guide the Dharma community. Retained public meaning is supported by independent present uses in recorded discourse.

Entries.SourceTerm: 師子窟中無異獸，象王行處絕狐蹤

Senses.PreferredTarget: No strange beasts live in the lion’s den; no fox tracks mark the elephant king’s path
SearchAliases: no strange beasts live in the lion’s den; no fox tracks mark the elephant king’s path
Senses.Note: When an emperor asks why Huayan Jing’s students are silent while others read, Jing answers that no other beast lives in a lion’s den and no fox track remains where an elephant king walks. Yezhu quotes the case and comments on Jing’s assembly. Yuechuang uses the same image to close a sermon about speaking before a public audience. Kaifu gives it as his own answer after asking how a teacher should respond, and Tanfang speaks it while taking up a new residence. The pair marks the force of a teaching presence, though its use depends on the speaker’s occasion.

Occurrences.Kwic: 高臥白雲，有時持盂鬧市，有時愛撫沒絃琴，有時善宣無量義，有時似癡似騃，有時為祥為瑞，不是碧眼胡，亦非傅大士。住！住！他秊自有知音知，何必清風動天地？上堂。秋日耀長空，秋江浸虗碧。傷嗟門外人，處處尋彌勒。驀路忽擡頭，相逢不相識。諸禪德，既是相逢，為什麼不相識？剪盡霜前竹，臨谿不化龍。擊禪牀。謝供頭化主，上堂。萬里無雲，長天一色，不落古今，那該彼此？要津把斷，風骨旋生。設使靈山密付，謾說拈華；少室親傳，徒誇得髓。總不恁麼，畢竟如何？要會麼？師子窟中無異獸，象王行處絕狐蹤。上堂，僧問：如何是事法界？師曰：杖子拈將來，隨時得受用。僧云：如何是理法界？師曰：玅體本無私，應緣非少剩。僧云：如何是理事無礙法界？師曰：通同歸實際，語玅少知音。僧云：如何是事事無礙法界？師曰：肥典座，瘦維那。師乃曰：薄󳺓明月碎清風，淺種深耕莫大功，破二作三橫豎算，四方八面用無窮。諸禪德！還委悉麼？當人分上在體前，不落偏圓，是何境界？放行也，諸佛放光明，助發實相義，言下合無生，為祥復為瑞。收來也，初祖門庭，不通水泄，無物堪比倫，教我如

Occurrences.Kwic: 固默相其前定者乎！今師年已七十，耳聰目明，視在蔣山時，尤為清徤，說法無虗日。繼此而編錄者，當不止此。傳錄之語，尚得而觀之。從茂之請，書此以為徑山語錄敘。至正三年歲癸未秋前奎章閣學士翰林侍講學士通奉大夫知制誥同脩國史雍郡虞集拜題。曇芳和尚杭州路徑山興聖萬壽禪寺語錄曇芳和尚杭州路徑山興聖萬壽禪寺語錄常州路善權禪寺住持嗣法繼祖等編師於至正二年歲壬午四月二十四日入院。據室，云：天下老和尚盡向者裏布縵天網、打鳳羅龍，新逕山合作麼生？拈主丈畫一畫：師子窟中無異獸，象王行處絕狐蹤。拈省臺院三疏，拈起示眾云：二千年前金口付囑，二千年後直為流通，風從虎兮雲從龍。指法座，云：向上一路，千聖不傳。今日新徑山放憨去也，須彌燈王且過那邊。遂陞，拈香云：此一瓣香爇向寶爐，端為祝延大元聖主今上皇帝聖躬萬歲萬歲萬萬歲，欽願陛下聖明如日月，睿筭等乾坤，八方歌有道之君，四海樂無為之化。次拈香云：此香爇向爐中，供養皇天之下一人之上西天佛子大元帝師大和尚殿下，恭願長為佛法之棟梁，永作皇朝之師範。次拈香云：此香爇向爐中，奉為江浙等處行中書

Senses.Explanation: A lion’s den and the path of an elephant king express a teacher’s ability to gather students without imitation. Yezhu reads the older Huayan Jing answer about his assembly; Yuechuang voices the line in a ceremonial sermon. Senses.Explanation: Literally, 末後一句 is ‘the final phrase.’ Yuanwu Keqin and Huishan Jiexian preserve the saying ‘with the final phrase, one first reaches the firm barrier,’ and Weilin Daopei quotes Luopu Yuanan expanding it: the crucial crossing is barred to ordinary and sage alike. Dongyuan Fazhen calls the final phrase the assembly's place to emerge, while Chaozong Tongren asks a monk for it and strikes after the reply. The Complete Five Lamps also preserves an unnamed monk asking Chengzhao Huici first for the first phrase and then for the final phrase, receiving a different answer to each. These sources treat it as a named verbal position that can be requested, stated, or appraised; they do not supply one universal final phrase.

Occurrences.ClaimText: 透脫末後牢關

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 故云末後一句始到牢關若一見不再見始覺即合本覺者自然透脫無疑
ClaimAnchors.AttributionNote: Source record (B/B27/B27n0152.xml). Recorded Sayings of National Master Puji Yulin (普濟玉琳國師語錄): Yulin Tongxiu is the exact speaker. ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 若識得此一問，便明最初一句，亦明末後一關，百千諸佛、百千戒法，盡從脚跟下流出。
ClaimAnchors.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X72/X72n1437.xml). Expanded Record of Chan Master Yongjue Yuanxian (永覺元賢禪師廣錄): Yongjue Yuanxian is the exact speaker. ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 若是末後一關，正未透在。眾中還有透得末後一關底麼？
ClaimAnchors.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J26/J26nB182.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Wanru (萬如禪師語錄): Wanru Tongwei is the exact speaker. Wanru Tongwei speaks from the hall, says earlier figures had not yet passed the final barrier, and asks whether anyone present has passed it.

Senses.Explanation: This is the final formidable barrier or severe checkpoint in a sequence of testing, something speakers say must be reached, passed through, or personally arrived at even after an earlier understanding. ‘Final’ marks its position and (牢) marks its formidable resistance; neither word by itself supplies the whole expression. The records speak of passing through or penetrating it, and use it as a severe last check. Yuan'an, after listing a series of named cases, calls "this whole tangle" (者一落索) the final locked barrier and criticizes estimating it through cognitive calculation. Juelang says even someone who has understood "this affair" but has "not passed through the final locked barrier" (未透末後牢關) can still mistake a shadow for a head. Yulin asks, "how many people have passed the final locked barrier?" (末後牢關幾人透得). Other formulations say it is "not measurable by humans or gods" (人天莫測) and "not understood by a thousand sages" (千聖不曉).

Senses.Note: This article limits the final barrier to the exact uses in J/J34/J34nB311.xml and J/J25/J25nB174.xml; no broader component count or neighbouring compound is used for validation.

Occurrences.Kwic: 室人王氏舉火為新豐孟嘉高居士室人王氏舉火舉火炬，云：「烈燄騰輝，朔風凜冽，快便難逢，好個時節。且道是甚麼時節？」呈火炬，云：「呵呵呵，咄咄咄，直教從此頓超越。」遂攛火炬，云：「咦！」為壽章禪人封龕為壽章禪人封龕師拈拄杖云：「秋雲縹緲，流水澄清，鐵鷂沖霄，泥牛入海，此正是壽章禪人歸根底時節。倘能如是知得落處，則生滅去來無影像，人間天上任逍遙；如或未然……」以拄杖指龕云：「好向其中明的旨，不須此外乞高超。」卓拄杖一下。舉火舉火舉火炬，云：「末後關頭須打徹，莫教枯坐便休歇，直得虛空血迸流，大地平沉方勦絕。」以火炬打○相，云：「吽。」遂攛下。為淨行者先考允升王公舉火為淨行者先考允升王公舉火舉火炬，云：「會得也，方知個事離生滅，桃李依然觸處開。如不薦，野衲當陽重指示，頓教從此脫塵埃。」喝一喝，遂攛下。為淨行者先母應氏孺人舉火為淨行者先母應氏孺人舉火舉火炬，云：「罪性如霜赫日臨，鐵圍粉碎竭迷津。急著眼，莫沉吟，看取蓮花火裡新。」打一○相，遂攛下。為行堅禪人下火為行堅禪人下火舉火炬，云：

Senses.Explanation: The “final barrier” is a named last checkpoint in the records. Masters ask whether it has been passed, place it after earlier barriers, or use it in verse; the phrase denotes that stated barrier, without supplying an outside theory of what passing it entails. Yichu urges breaking through the final gate in his own fire verse for a deceased practitioner.

Senses.PreferredTarget: In the latter age of the teaching, many have only dry wisdom.
AlternateTargets: As the teaching declines, dry understanding is widespread.
SearchAliases: dry understanding in the decline of teaching
Senses.Note: Dongshan Liangjie warns Caoshan that the latter age will have many people with dry wisdom, then names three leaks of seeing, emotion, and speech. Sanshan comments on each leak; Wenmu answers them in a new verse. Yingning brings the warning into a dispute about what counts as genuine transmission. Pinjixiang says even such dry understanding has become scarce and asks his disciples how the leaks are avoided. Dry wisdom here is insight that has not become dependable conduct.

Occurrences.Kwic: 喬松展化機，奼女驚回霜夜夢，倒騎鐵馬趁雲飛。投子大同禪師，因僧問：「和尚住此山有何境界？」子曰：「丫角女子白頭絲。」碧巖深處響寒蛩，丹桂凝霜濕翠容，佩玉嫦娥歌舞後，畫堂月落彩雲籠。德山宣鑒禪師晚參：「今夜不荅話，問話者三十棒。」時有僧出禮拜，山便打。僧曰：「某甲話也未問，和尚因甚便打？」山曰：「你是甚處人？」僧曰：「新羅人。」山曰：「未跨船舷，好與三十棒。」靈峰驀為展，神用詎能量，非獨妖氛掃，此中更有長。洞山良价禪師，解夏上堂：「初秋夏末，兄弟東去西去，直須向萬里無寸草處去。」良久，曰：「祇如萬里無寸草處，作麼生去？」顧左右，曰：「欲知此事，直須枯木上生花方與他合。」鳳舞庭梧金鴨襲，龍吟碧沼錦雲攢，回途復妙尊嚴甚，夜月流輝古殿寒。洞山因僧問：「寒暑到來，如何回避？」山曰：「何不向無寒暑處去？」僧曰：「如何是無寒暑處？」山曰：「寒時寒殺闍黎，熱時熱殺闍黎。」太古琴彈世絕聽，五音不犯妙殊深，僊陀秘術誠難跡，別館時聞漏已沉。洞山曰：「末法時代，人多乾慧。若要辨驗真偽，有三種滲漏：一曰見滲漏，機不離位，墮在毒海；二曰情滲漏，滯在向背，見處偏枯；三曰語滲漏，究妙失宗，機昧始終，濁智流轉。」洞開劫運渺難符，照盡功忘尚墮諸，類既莫齊猶卓爾，銀籠鶴出井梧舒。仰山慧寂禪師。因僧問：「如何是祖師意？」山於空作󱐞相示之，僧無語。上有千尺桐，下有千尺井，風吹井上桐，零落井中影。九峰道虔禪師，因僧問：「如何是頭？」峰曰：「開眼不覺曉。」曰：「如何是尾？」峰曰：「不坐萬年床。」曰：「有頭無尾時如何？」峰曰：「終是不貴。」曰：「有尾無頭時如何？」峰曰：「雖飽無力。」曰：「直得頭尾相稱時如何？」峰曰：「兒孫得力，室內不知。」迢迢劫外復何期？枯木回春妙轉機，五馬不嘶偏正合，苔生玉殿月含輝。巖頭全奯禪師示眾：「吾教意猶如塗毒鼓，擊一聲遠近聞者皆喪。」時有小嚴上座出問：「如何是塗毒鼓？」巖以兩手按膝亞身，云：「韓信臨朝底。」嚴無語。庭松巖桂影婆娑，叫月玄猿出薜蘿，山色溪光雖未隔，就中謾道不淆訛。曹山本寂禪師，因僧問：「子歸就父，為甚麼父全不顧？」山曰：「理合如是。」曰：「父子之恩何在？」山曰：「始成父子之恩。」曰：「如何是父子之恩？」山曰：「刀斧斫不開。」霜凝古木倚寒鴉，疏影橫斜隔亮紗，翡翠簾垂紅日隱，

Occurrences.Kwic: 靜鞭響徹三更已，玉露重添虎帳雲。宮漏沉沉紫氣濃，五更霜冷浸人風。朝臣待曉金階底，差與龍顏咫尺逢。機到誰分主與賓，蟭螟驅起石麒麟。萬年松老無人到，挂角羚羊不可尋。隱顯全該意氣和，相逢俱喜唱巴歌。閒聽八拍胡笳裏，吹出鄉關夢幾多。」僧問：「雲門綱宗頌中曰：『咄咄咄！力韋希，禪子訝，中眉垂。』者箇頌子竟無啟口處，不識是何道理？」師曰：「者一首且置，餘頌還理會得麼？」僧曰：「餘者還得。」師曰：「只如末後頌曰：『笑我者多，哂我者少。』你作麼生會？」僧擬議，師曰：「又是蚊子上銕牛。」遂為頌曰：「咄咄咄！四圍八表清風度。力韋希，擬議之間墮銕圍。禪子訝，寒山忘卻舊時家。中眉垂，燄裏冰花發幾回。笑我者多、知我者少，鬥湊將來卻也恰好。風雨無端弄曉春，殘花落盡無人掃。」示門人語曰：「吾宗的旨，事不尋常。如洞山价祖謂曹山曰：『吾在雲巖先師處，親印寶鏡三昧，事窮的要，今以授汝。汝善護持，無令斷絕，遇真法器，方可傳授。直須秘密，不可彰露，恐屬流布，喪滅吾宗。末法時代，人多乾慧。若要辯驗向上人之真偽，有三種滲漏，直須具眼。一見滲漏，二情滲漏，三語滲漏。』此是洞山親囑曹山語也。今時學此道者，不惟具向上機，透脫法身者難得，即乾慧人亦不多見。諸方提持此宗者，每見土曠人稀，便就機境上接伊。學家多是起模畫樣，向印板上脫來，所以不得光大門風。故山僧無時不切切傷懷，爾輩幸宜勉旃。」僧曰：「如師所述三種滲漏，敢望慈悲歡喜法施。如何得見不滲漏？」師曰：「直須足下無私去，拈起南辰打北辰。」「如何得情不滲漏？」師曰：「要從凡聖機先舉，纔有些毫便著他。」「如何得語不滲漏？」師曰：「妙舞自來無著處，青山直得輾為塵。」復以頌示曰：「浪潑蘆花懶繫船，白雲空蕩水中天。東西兩岸無人已，援取琵琶去卻絃。少小離家不著憂，逢場慣喜作風流。月明沽得三升酒，洗盡平生數丈愁。忙殺街頭石敢當，東家一事惱人腸。夜深走出貓兒了，老鼠偷油打破缸。」師舉：「先雲峰悅禪師曰：『肇法師道：「智有窮幽之鑑而無知焉，神有應會之用而無慮焉。」古人與麼道也太煞費力，爭如諸上座寒即圍爐向火，熱即竹林溪畔坐？雖然如是，我且問你：畢竟事作麼生？』」師曰：「先雲峰只知瞻前，不解顧後，事有甚麼畢竟不畢竟？若果有畢竟事，則成知成慮矣。據山僧見處，只好道箇無事出門忘計較，逢人便
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J39/J39nB454.xml). Recorded sayings. Pinjixiang quotes Dongshan to his disciples, says even dry understanding is scarce, and answers questions on all three leaks.

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 喬松展化機，奼女驚回霜夜夢，倒騎鐵馬趁雲飛。投子大同禪師，因僧問：「和尚住此山有何境界？」子曰：「丫角女子白頭絲。」碧巖深處響寒蛩，丹桂凝霜濕翠容，佩玉嫦娥歌舞後，畫堂月落彩雲籠。德山宣鑒禪師晚參：「今夜不荅話，問話者三十棒。」時有僧出禮拜，山便打。僧曰：「某甲話也未問，和尚因甚便打？」山曰：「你是甚處人？」僧曰：「新羅人。」山曰：「未跨船舷，好與三十棒。」靈峰驀為展，神用詎能量，非獨妖氛掃，此中更有長。洞山良价禪師，解夏上堂：「初秋夏末，兄弟東去西去，直須向萬里無寸草處去。」良久，曰：「祇如萬里無寸草處，作麼生去？」顧左右，曰：「欲知此事，直須枯木上生花方與他合。」鳳舞庭梧金鴨襲，龍吟碧沼錦雲攢，回途復妙尊嚴甚，夜月流輝古殿寒。洞山因僧問：「寒暑到來，如何回避？」山曰：「何不向無寒暑處去？」僧曰：「如何是無寒暑處？」山曰：「寒時寒殺闍黎，熱時熱殺闍黎。」太古琴彈世絕聽，五音不犯妙殊深，僊陀秘術誠難跡，別館時聞漏已沉。洞山曰：「末法時代，人多乾慧。若要辨驗真偽，有三種滲漏：一曰見滲漏，機不離位，墮在毒海；二曰情滲漏，滯在向背，見處偏枯；三曰語滲漏，究妙失宗，機昧始終，濁智流轉。」洞開劫運渺難符，照盡功忘尚墮諸，類既莫齊猶卓爾，銀籠鶴出井梧舒。仰山慧寂禪師。因僧問：「如何是祖師意？」山於空作󱐞相示之，僧無語。上有千尺桐，下有千尺井，風吹井上桐，零落井中影。九峰道虔禪師，因僧問：「如何是頭？」峰曰：「開眼不覺曉。」曰：「如何是尾？」峰曰：「不坐萬年床。」曰：「有頭無尾時如何？」峰曰：「終是不貴。」曰：「有尾無頭時如何？」峰曰：「雖飽無力。」曰：「直得頭尾相稱時如何？」峰曰：「兒孫得力，室內不知。」迢迢劫外復何期？枯木回春妙轉機，五馬不嘶偏正合，苔生玉殿月含輝。巖頭全奯禪師示眾：「吾教意猶如塗毒鼓，擊一聲遠近聞者皆喪。」時有小嚴上座出問：「如何是塗毒鼓？」巖以兩手按膝亞身，云：「韓信臨朝底。」嚴無語。庭松巖桂影婆娑，叫月玄猿出薜蘿，山色溪光雖未隔，就中謾道不淆訛。曹山本寂禪師，因僧問：「子歸就父，為甚麼父全不顧？」山曰：「理合如是。」曰：「父子之恩何在？」山曰：「始成父子之恩。」曰：「如何是父子之恩？」山曰：「刀斧斫不開。」霜凝古木倚寒鴉，疏影橫斜隔亮紗，翡翠簾垂紅日隱，

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 靜鞭響徹三更已，玉露重添虎帳雲。宮漏沉沉紫氣濃，五更霜冷浸人風。朝臣待曉金階底，差與龍顏咫尺逢。機到誰分主與賓，蟭螟驅起石麒麟。萬年松老無人到，挂角羚羊不可尋。隱顯全該意氣和，相逢俱喜唱巴歌。閒聽八拍胡笳裏，吹出鄉關夢幾多。」僧問：「雲門綱宗頌中曰：『咄咄咄！力韋希，禪子訝，中眉垂。』者箇頌子竟無啟口處，不識是何道理？」師曰：「者一首且置，餘頌還理會得麼？」僧曰：「餘者還得。」師曰：「只如末後頌曰：『笑我者多，哂我者少。』你作麼生會？」僧擬議，師曰：「又是蚊子上銕牛。」遂為頌曰：「咄咄咄！四圍八表清風度。力韋希，擬議之間墮銕圍。禪子訝，寒山忘卻舊時家。中眉垂，燄裏冰花發幾回。笑我者多、知我者少，鬥湊將來卻也恰好。風雨無端弄曉春，殘花落盡無人掃。」示門人語曰：「吾宗的旨，事不尋常。如洞山价祖謂曹山曰：『吾在雲巖先師處，親印寶鏡三昧，事窮的要，今以授汝。汝善護持，無令斷絕，遇真法器，方可傳授。直須秘密，不可彰露，恐屬流布，喪滅吾宗。末法時代，人多乾慧。若要辯驗向上人之真偽，有三種滲漏，直須具眼。一見滲漏，二情滲漏，三語滲漏。』此是洞山親囑曹山語也。今時學此道者，不惟具向上機，透脫法身者難得，即乾慧人亦不多見。諸方提持此宗者，每見土曠人稀，便就機境上接伊。學家多是起模畫樣，向印板上脫來，所以不得光大門風。故山僧無時不切切傷懷，爾輩幸宜勉旃。」僧曰：「如師所述三種滲漏，敢望慈悲歡喜法施。如何得見不滲漏？」師曰：「直須足下無私去，拈起南辰打北辰。」「如何得情不滲漏？」師曰：「要從凡聖機先舉，纔有些毫便著他。」「如何得語不滲漏？」師曰：「妙舞自來無著處，青山直得輾為塵。」復以頌示曰：「浪潑蘆花懶繫船，白雲空蕩水中天。東西兩岸無人已，援取琵琶去卻絃。少小離家不著憂，逢場慣喜作風流。月明沽得三升酒，洗盡平生數丈愁。忙殺街頭石敢當，東家一事惱人腸。夜深走出貓兒了，老鼠偷油打破缸。」師舉：「先雲峰悅禪師曰：『肇法師道：「智有窮幽之鑑而無知焉，神有應會之用而無慮焉。」古人與麼道也太煞費力，爭如諸上座寒即圍爐向火，熱即竹林溪畔坐？雖然如是，我且問你：畢竟事作麼生？』」師曰：「先雲峰只知瞻前，不解顧後，事有甚麼畢竟不畢竟？若果有畢竟事，則成知成慮矣。據山僧見處，只好道箇無事出門忘計較，逢人便

Senses.Explanation: The compact warning names dry wisdom as a danger in the later age of the teaching. Sanshan and Wenmu treat the following three leaks as concrete tests of seeing, feeling, and speech. Yingning uses the warning in a lineage dispute; Pinjixiang challenges his own disciples to answer the three leaks.

This is the graph variant of the traditional spelling of “cat”. The dominant Zen deployment is Nanquan's cat case: the eastern and western halls fight over the cat, Nanquan says that speaking will save it and failure to speak will mean its cutting, the assembly gives no answer, and the record says he cuts it. Zhaozhou later places a straw sandal on his head, after which Nanquan says he would have saved the cat. Beyond that case, the corpus uses the same word for ordinary mouse-catching cats and records Luohan Xinglin Zuyin lifting a live cat before the assembly while explicitly recalling Nanquan.
Senses.Note: Later commentary preserves a factual and evaluative dispute. The Book of Serenity reports that one critic reproached Nanquan's group for "killing living beings and creating guilt" (殺生造罪), while a defender cited an old text in which Nanquan made only a simulated cutting gesture (以手作虛斫勢). The commentary then evaluates the two critics; this entry records the controversy without choosing between the transmitted narratives or assigning an unstated intention. The traditional spelling of “cat” is a separate searchable entry with the same sense.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J34/J34nB300.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Chaozong. Chaozong Tongren explains how different doctrinal distinctions need not divide the matter they describe. Discussing the four fields of the Flower Garland teaching, he says that each particular event enters all events and all events enter each one; whichever field is raised for the needs of an occasion, the others are complete within it. He compares this to a ring without an end and to scattering pearls inside a purple gauze enclosure, asking where one could set one's eye. He then criticizes people who repeat a few dead formulas and claim to have gone beyond doctrinal reasoning. Here the scattered pearls image belongs to mutually complete perspectives that resist a separately fixed viewing point, not merely to ornament concealing an answer. Chaozong is the present speaker; the subsequent question about earlier interpretations of Linji is another turn.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (C/C078/C078n1720.xml). Chan School: Comprehensive Linked-Pearls Collection of Verse Commentaries on Old Cases. An inline source note attributes this four-line verse to Lingyan An, whose fuller identity is not established here. The poem places distinguishing the wild fox before Baizhang's hall beside scattering pearls in a purple gauze enclosure, then asks whose separate residence has a pond where a pair of mandarin ducks float. The surrounding collection gathers many different authors' responses to the fox case, including its contrast between not falling under cause and effect and not obscuring cause and effect; those neighboring verses are not all Lingyan An's speech. His own four lines move from the difficult discrimination to concealed pearls and the paired birds, without explaining a fixed correspondence for each image. The verse should therefore remain a pointed, compressed response to that case, rather than being made to settle its causal question in explanatory prose.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J25/J25nB171.xml). Recorded Sayings of Monk Tianyin. Tianyin Yuanxiu raises Shoushan's answer to a monk asking what Buddha is: a bride rides the donkey while her mother-in-law leads it. When the monk asks which category of sentence can contain it, Shoushan says neither the three mysteries nor the four sentences can encompass it, then answers with the enduring heaven and earth and the sun and moon shining together. Tianyin asks his assembly whether they recognize Shoushan scattering pearls within a purple gauze enclosure. A separate unnamed monk then asks what this pearl-scattering is. Tianyin replies by putting the same family scene in a different order, the mother-in-law leading and the bride riding, and warns the monk not to invent forced explanations. The retained passage thus has two actual voices speaking the headword: Tianyin's present question and the monk's follow-up. Tianyin remains the respondent; neither the family image nor the pearl image is assigned a hidden code by his reply.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J27/J27nB197.xml). Essentials of the Recorded Sayings of Master Wu Yi of Boshan. Wuyi Yuanlai recounts Linji asking Huangbo three times for the deepest meaning of the teaching and receiving blows each time. Linji then tells Dayu that he does not know whether he had a fault; Dayu calls Huangbo's treatment grandmotherly kindness, and Linji awakens. Wuyi describes the force of the blows and asks why Linji later shouted at people indiscriminately. Without scattering pearls within the purple gauze enclosure, he says, one remains a shrimp unable to leap out of its measure. The image thus marks something that noisy imitation alone cannot supply: his criticism asks how the realized encounter works, rather than treating shouting as its sufficient result. Wuyi is the present speaker applying the image, not an unnamed participant in Linji's earlier encounter.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J33/J33nB286.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Yingningjing. Yingning Zhijing addresses the assembly with a bright round light and a break through a dim barrier, then says that pearls are being scattered inside the purple gauze enclosure and challenges those with eyes to speak. Two monks compete to emerge. He says one has gained and one lost; when both shout, he calls them people caught with stolen goods while protesting injustice. One protests that the teacher should not turn an innocent person into a criminal, and Yingning takes his staff and drives them out of the hall. Returning to his seat, he speaks of two colors in one contest and warns a true intimate not to remain outside the gate. The pearl image announces a present test whose value is not exhausted by the monks' competitive performance. The passage does not identify a winner for the reader to imitate.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J34/J34nB301.xml). Recorded Sayings of Monk Jiqi of Nanyue. Jiqi Hongchu first assigns different kinds of response different seats and honors, then raises a monk asking the National Teacher for the Buddha of illumination in person. The teacher tells him to bring the water pitcher and then return it to its former place. When the monk repeats his question, the teacher says that the ancient Buddha has long passed away. Jiqi tells those who have not understood to watch him scatter pearls inside the purple gauze enclosure, adding that even so, those who understand are rare. After a pause he says 'Gather it in' and ends the address. The image applies to the teaching being offered through the ordinary pitcher actions and the unanswered demand for another explanation; it does not reveal a separate object hidden behind those actions. Jiqi is the current speaker assessing the raised exchange.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J32/J32nB272.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Hongzhi Jue of Tiantong Jingde Monastery, Mingzhou. Hongzhi Zhengjue opens an address with curtains hanging in the yellow pavilion and asks who carries the family message. The purple gauze enclosure is closed, he says, while true pearls are scattered unseen. He then makes the difficulty explicit: sight and hearing do not reach here, and words cannot convey it, so how can news get through? His closing lines turn from this obscured transmission to waking as night begins to lighten and smilingly pointing to the family's springtime flourishing. The pearl image is therefore part of a present question about how the teaching becomes apparent when its usual channels fail. Hongzhi does not end by declaring communication impossible; nor does he explain the pearls as literal objects hidden inside a room.

Occurrences.Kwic: 粜却。󳳟賓雖乘快便，爭柰白折一隻臂。舉文殊問疾，論不二法門，維摩默然。拈，大士默然，直得山河大地、草木藂林，情與無情共轉根本法輪，非惟文殊贊嘆不及，任是古今佛祖競出頭來亦無啟口處。美則美矣，點檢將來也是持鉢不得。舉：障蔽魔王一千年，不見金剛齊菩薩。拈金剛齊瞞障蔽魔王即得，衲僧門下喫棒趂出有分。何故？兩手扶犁水過膝。舉七賢女遊尸陀林。拈聖女作麼？作麼？認驢鞍橋作阿爺下頷，引得諸姊束手墮懸崖。帝釋既知善說般若，因甚三件物會麼？自從掣得金鰲後，更不晴江理釣絲。舉：城東老母與佛同生，不愿見佛。拈。城東老母，太煞老婆。既不柰何，與渠同生。何用苦苦，作麼要好？日日香花夜夜燈，教渠自知慚愧去。何故？見怪不怪，其怪自壞。釋迦老子可謂貴買賤賣，他既不要便休，何苦亞渠作麼？遂顧左右，召大眾云：還見釋迦老子麼？自云：在這裏。乃云：無事提瓶挈水去。舉：鹽官問座主：華嚴有幾重法界？主云：略有四重，廣則重重無盡。官提起拂子云：這个是第幾重？主良久，官云：思而知，慮而解，鬼家活計。日下孤燈，果然失照。拈舉：諸方拈提了，乃云：諸方老宿只解扶強，不能扶弱，殊不知這僧良久，華嚴法界如帝網交羅，重重攝入，說甚麼第幾重？會麼？但見皇風成一片，不知何處是封疆？舉，達磨謂門人曰：時將至矣，汝自各言所得。拈云：三千弟子鴛行立，一一呼來教順朱。達磨大師如弄棚頭傀儡，雖則語言進退，雍容可觀，殊不知用盡自己心，笑破他人口。舉：僧問曹山：抱璞投師，乞師雕琢。曹云：不雕琢。僧云：因甚不雕琢？曹云：須信曹山好手。拈：黃閣簾垂，難傳信息；紫羅帳合，暗撒真珠。曹洞家風，可謂綿密，子細看來，猶欠大人相在。山僧即不然，忽有問：抱璞投師，乞師雕琢。即向道：侍者寮喫茶去。忽然瞥地，󳬧子已過新羅國。舉雲門問僧：甚處來？僧云：岳山來也。門云：老僧不曾與人葛藤。僧珍重便出，門喚云：近前來。僧近前，門云：去。徑山拈云：葛藤不少。拈得也，得也。舉：雪峰示眾云：雪峰門下不得咳嗽。時有僧咳嗽一聲，峰云：作恁麼？僧云：傷風。峰云：傷風即得。拈雷聲浩大，雨點全無。舉洞山示眾：秋初夏末，東去西去，直須向萬里無寸草處去。石霜道：出門便是草。拈一人平地上險崕，一人險崕中平地，點檢將來，總欠一著。萬里無寸草，出門便是草，支笻寂寞中，望斷無人到。舉，李殿撰問雪竇云：三教中那个㝡尊？竇起身側立。撰云：有口何不道？竇云：對夫子以難言。拈三教誰尊，側身而立。當門不用㘽荊棘，對夫子以難言。賊，賊！舉：忠國師問紫璘供奉：佛是什麼義？奉云：是覺義。師云：佛曾迷否？云：不曾迷。師云：用覺什麼？奉無對。拈。不因樵子徑，爭到葛洪家。又。家無小使。舉：忠國師云：語漸也，返常合道；語頓也，不留眹迹。大慧喝一喝，云：寐語作什麼？遂舉拂子，復彈指，云：徑山即今舉拂彈指，若向這裡覔眹迹，入地獄如箭射。拈寐語不少。舉：歸宗因僧問：如何是佛？宗云：我與汝道，恐汝不信。僧云：和尚誠言，焉敢不信？宗云：只汝是。僧云：如何保任？宗云：一翳在眼，空花徧界。僧於此有省。拈歸宗為人，雖無迃曲，點檢將來，大似嚼飯餧孩兒，當是个漢。待他道只你是，便掩耳而出，教這老漢開口了合不得。舉：清原令石頭與大慧通書，乃云：回來

Caoshan refuses, then says the monk must trust that Caoshan is a good craftsman. In his own appraisal Xisou takes up the yellow pavilion with curtains down and news difficult to transmit, followed by the closed purple gauze enclosure and pearls scattered unseen. He calls this the fine density of the Cao-Dong house, then judges that it still lacks the bearing of a fully grown person. He proposes another reply to the request for carving: go drink tea in the attendants' quarters. If there is suddenly an awakening, he adds, the fellow has already gone beyond Silla. He does not name Hongzhi as the speaker of his appraisal, and the headword belongs to Xisou's current revoicing.

Senses.Explanation: Pearls scattered within a purple gauze enclosure picture something offered yet difficult to discern; the teachers put this image to different tests and sometimes criticize its manner of concealment. Chaozong Tongren explains how different doctrinal distinctions need not divide the matter they describe. Discussing the four fields of the Flower Garland teaching, he says that each particular event enters all events and all events enter each one; whichever field is raised for the needs of an occasion, the others are complete within it. He compares this to a ring without an end and to scattering pearls inside a purple gauze enclosure, asking where one could set one's eye. He then criticizes people who repeat a few dead formulas and claim to have gone beyond doctrinal reasoning. Here the scattered pearls image belongs to mutually complete perspectives that resist a separately fixed viewing point, not merely to ornament concealing an answer. Chaozong is the present speaker; the subsequent question about earlier interpretations of Linji is another turn. An inline source note attributes this four-line verse to Lingyan An, whose fuller identity is not established here. The poem places distinguishing the wild fox before Baizhang's hall beside scattering pearls in a purple gauze enclosure, then asks whose separate residence has a pond where a pair of mandarin ducks float. The surrounding collection gathers many different authors' responses to the fox case, including its contrast between not falling under cause and effect and not obscuring cause and effect; those neighboring verses are not all Lingyan An's speech. His own four lines move from the difficult discrimination to concealed pearls and the paired birds, without explaining a fixed correspondence for each image. The verse should therefore remain a pointed, compressed response to that case, rather than being made to settle its causal question in explanatory prose. Tianyin Yuanxiu raises Shoushan's answer to a monk asking what Buddha is: a bride rides the donkey while her mother-in-law leads it. When the monk asks which category of sentence can contain it, Shoushan says neither the three mysteries nor the four sentences can encompass it, then answers with the enduring heaven and earth and the sun and moon shining together. Tianyin asks his assembly whether they recognize Shoushan scattering pearls within a purple gauze enclosure. A separate unnamed monk then asks what this pearl-scattering is. Tianyin replies by putting the same family scene in a different order, the mother-in-law leading and the bride riding, and warns the monk not to invent forced explanations. The retained passage thus has two actual voices speaking the headword: Tianyin's present question and the monk's follow-up. Tianyin remains the respondent; neither the family image nor the pearl image is assigned a hidden code by his reply. Wuyi Yuanlai recounts Linji asking Huangbo three times for the deepest meaning of the teaching and receiving blows each time. Linji then tells Dayu that he does not know whether he had a fault; Dayu calls Huangbo's treatment grandmotherly kindness, and Linji awakens. Wuyi describes the force of the blows and asks why Linji later shouted at people indiscriminately. Without scattering pearls within the purple gauze enclosure, he says, one remains a shrimp unable to leap out of its measure. The image thus marks something that noisy imitation alone cannot supply: his criticism asks how the realized encounter works, rather than treating shouting as its sufficient result. Wuyi is the present speaker applying the image, not an unnamed participant in Linji's earlier encounter. Yingning Zhijing addresses the assembly with a bright round light and a break through a dim barrier, then says that pearls are being scattered inside the purple gauze enclosure and challenges those with eyes to speak. Two monks compete to emerge. He says one has gained and one lost; when both shout, he calls them people caught with stolen goods while protesting injustice. One protests that the teacher should not turn an innocent person into a criminal, and Yingning takes his staff and drives them out of the hall. Returning to his seat, he speaks of two colors in one contest and warns a true intimate not to remain outside the gate. The pearl image announces a present test whose value is not exhausted by the monks' competitive performance. The passage does not identify a winner for the reader to imitate. Jiqi Hongchu first assigns different kinds of response different seats and honors, then raises a monk asking the National Teacher for the Buddha of illumination in person. The teacher tells him to bring the water pitcher and then return it to its former place. When the monk repeats his question, the teacher says that the ancient Buddha has long passed away. Jiqi tells those who have not understood to watch him scatter pearls inside the purple gauze enclosure, adding that even so, those who understand are rare. After a pause he says 'Gather it in' and ends the address. The image applies to the teaching being offered through the ordinary pitcher actions and the unanswered demand for another explanation; it does not reveal a separate object hidden behind those actions. Jiqi is the current speaker assessing the raised exchange. Hongzhi Zhengjue opens an address with curtains hanging in the yellow pavilion and asks who carries the family message. The purple gauze enclosure is closed, he says, while true pearls are scattered unseen. He then makes the difficulty explicit: sight and hearing do not reach here, and words cannot convey it, so how can news get through? His closing lines turn from this obscured transmission to waking as night begins to lighten and smilingly pointing to the family's springtime flourishing. The pearl image is therefore part of a present question about how the teaching becomes apparent when its usual channels fail. Hongzhi does not end by declaring communication impossible; nor does he explain the pearls as literal objects hidden inside a room. He calls this the fine density of the Cao-Dong house, then judges that it still lacks the bearing of a fully grown person. He proposes another reply to the request for carving: go drink tea in the attendants' quarters. If there is suddenly an awakening, he adds, the fellow has already gone beyond Silla. The pearl image now names a manner of teaching that Xisou appreciates yet criticizes and replaces with his own ordinary directive. He does not name Hongzhi as the speaker of his appraisal, and the headword belongs to Xisou's current revoicing.

Purple Fungus Song (紫芝歌) has 21 hits in 19 texts; gathering purple fungus (採紫芝) occurs once. Senses.Explanation: Dafang Xinghai's mountain verse is the corpus's direct plant action: he is too indolent to gather purple fungus beside the stream (懶去溪邊採紫芝). The plant-name circulates much more widely in the compound Purple Fungus Song. Tiantong Shanxin is publicly asked what that song is and answers by clapping; Fahua Quanju answers an independent transmission of the question by saying that it is not a Wu sound but must be Han speech (不是吳音切湏漢語). Yongjue Yuanxian asks who will join a solitary recluse in singing it (中有幽人守貞獨，誰來同唱紫芝歌), Xisou Shaotan places groups of two and three singing it on stones under pine roots (三三兩兩松根石上唱紫芝歌), and Yuanwu Keqin asks who can sing it in the season of high mountains, autumn wind, and a single goose (誰當此時節。解唱紫芝歌。). Wuwen Daocan separately invokes the Four Hoaryheads of Mount Shang and their heart of withdrawal, but his verse does not contain the headword. Zen bends the plant-name into a song asked about in public interviews and sung in mountain-retreat verse. The evidence does not make the bare word itself the title of a second thing.

Senses.Explanation: The phrase means to shed or stand free of the faculties and their objects. Yongjue Yuanxian supplies the corpus's explicit parsing: the mind that affirms is the faculty, and the object affirmed is the object-dust. Yongjue uses the phrase while explaining Baizhang's sudden summons, then contrasts Yantou's warning that affirmation has not escaped faculty and object. Letan Yingqian's hall address pairs radiant light with standing free of them. The Baozang Lun wording quoted by Wansong asks when the priceless treasure will shine alone and escape them. Mingjue Cong, Yuanwu Keqin, and Doushuai Congyue use the phrase in a birthday verse, direct instruction, and enthronement address.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J28/J28nB205.xml). Recorded Sayings of Chan Master Jieweizhou Xingzhou. Speaker: Jieweizhou Xingzhou in a memorial small address. This longer-object family passage explains the entry but does not count toward bare-headword depth.

Senses.Explanation: To be free of birth and death is a recurrent aim and test-question in the records. Doushuai Congyue says that after recognizing one's own nature one can be free of birth and death, then immediately asks how one is free when the eyes fall shut and where one goes when the four elements separate. Daxiu Zhu and later interview records preserve the same demand for an answer rather than treating the phrase as self-explanatory. Jieweizhou Xingzhou gives the clearest internal description: when birth is not taken as pleasure and death is not taken as suffering, so that pleasure and suffering do not constrain one, he calls this being free of the appearance of birth-and-death's coming and going.

Senses.Explanation: To slip off the halter: an image of release from constraining views and learned burdens. Yongjue describes helping others escape the halter of doctrinal interpretation; Xutang and Gulin use it in present sermons; Yuanwu pairs it with unloading the pack in his own Blue Cliff introduction. Retained public meaning is supported by independent present uses in recorded discourse.

Senses.Note: In these uses the expression intensifies speaking, accord, completion, taking up, departure, or disclosure; it does not by itself assert literal abandonment of a physical body.

Occurrences.AttributionNote: Source record (J/J10/J10nA158.xml). Recorded Sayings of Miyun Yuanwu (密雲禪師語錄): Miyun Yuanwu pairs fallen leaves with complete disclosure through-and-through and clouds clearing before the noon sun.

Senses.Explanation: Through-and-through. Shangfeng Bencai's formula contrasts the relative ease of emerging from one's situation with the difficulty of speaking through-and-through. Feiyin Tongrong applies the same force to conduct after former valuables have been dropped, and Yinyuan Longqi to taking the matter up completely. Chaozong Tongren joins the term to completion, Yushan Shangsi to accord, Guishan Zhe to departing free, and Miyun Yuanwu to full disclosure. The changing predicates preserve one intensifying job rather than seven separate things. Zen bends a bodily image into a demand with no protected remainder. The corpus tests whether speech, accord, responsibility, or manifestation is complete in the whole person, not merely asserted in part.

Senses.Explanation: “At a loss” describes visible failure to find an answer or footing. Yongming Yanshou describes Ananda as at a loss through seven examinations; the Chan Gate’s Treasure Store warns that someone without settled contemplation will be at a loss; Yuanwu Keqin says many students become at a loss when questioned; and Dawei Jinglun applies the word in direct instruction. A strong encounter narrates an unnamed monk’s reaction, while one lamp recension preserves an assembled group’s collective reaction.

Entries.SourceTerm: 茫茫宇宙人無數，那箇男兒是丈夫

Senses.PreferredTarget: Countless people fill the vast world; which one is a person of real resolve?
AlternateTargets: In this boundless world there are innumerable people; which of them stands as a true person?
SearchAliases: countless people vast world true person Zen
which person has real resolve Chan
Senses.Note: The question sets a vast crowd against the one person who can meet the moment. Shaweng uses it as his example of a living phrase. Gusu challenges his assembly with it, Hengshan asks it after a monk’s exchange, and Pingshi puts it into a verse about Fish-Basket Guanyin. Here the words for man (男兒) and worthy person (丈夫) ask for courage and capacity in the encounter, not a count of men in the room.

Occurrences.Kwic: 合節，左右逢原，尊卑異位，開鑿人天正眼，󳭪張佛祖門庭，頭頭垂應物之機，著著有出身之路，如斯話會，猶落今時。且如何是不落今時底句？玲瓏八面自回合，峭峻一方誰敢窺？上堂，舉：密菴和尚示眾云：十五日已前，開池不待月；十五日已後，池成月自來；正當十五日，吹無孔笛、唱太平歌，佛及眾生齊聲唱和。且超群拔萃一句作麼生道？四海浪平龍睡穩，九天雲淨鶴飛高。師云：山僧今日因行，不妨掉臂。十五日已前，長在途中，不離家舍；十五日已後，長在家舍，不離途中；正當十五日，兩頭俱坐斷，一劒倚天寒。且超群拔萃一句作麼生道？擊拂子：一把柳絲收不得，和煙搭在玉欄干。退院，上堂。老向山中償宿債，拖犁拽耙十三年，如今筋骨條條露，鼻孔頑然不受穿。村草步，舊田園，桃花如錦柳如煙，放教臥月眠雲去，飢有青蒭渴有泉。拍禪牀，下座。真讚真讚門人師楷文斌汝均等編觀音觀音枯木巖前坐片時，輪珠數盡復思惟。南詢童子無消息，月在波心說向誰。魚籃觀音魚籃觀音籃裡魚，衣內珠。左提右挈，腥風滿途。茫茫宇宙人無數，那箇男兒是丈夫。達磨達磨聖諦廓然，忠言逆耳。折蘆渡江，事不獲已。脚下無風帀帀波，滔天沃日從茲始。寒山寒山天台山中，國清寺裡。掃󰆠隨身，塵埃滿地。只知指點笑他人，對面有人還笑你。拾得拾得爾名拾得，拾得者誰？不識一字，却要題詩。禿筆未曾輕點著，芭蕉葉上墨淋漓。維摩維摩嘆大褒圓，彈偏擊小。通身是病，自救不了。引得文殊問疾來，狼籍一場非小小。朝陽穿破衲朝陽穿破衲穴鼻針，無絲線。蹙斷雙眉，討頭未見。日炙風吹破衲衣，補得完全是幾時。對月了殘經對月了殘經看未了，歇不得，向下文長，付在來日。咄！者醃黑荳老僧，何曾解轉如是經？船子船子天無四壁地無門，舞棹呈橈誑後昆。索性和船都覆却，免教空記刻舟痕。永明壽禪師永明壽禪師道大德尊，宗通眼活，萬象森羅，熾然而說。游戲性海而一波不驚，披露覺天而十日竝出，實天台韶國師命世之寧馨，作兩浙錢大王福田之利益。至於秉五色筆，發佛祖潛光；鼓無絃琴，起衲僧痼疾。高風遠度，豐功偉蹟，豈片言隻字讚歎之所能及？咦！面目分明不覆藏，西湖水映中巖月。延慶秋墟入法師延慶秋墟入法師秋水兮澄神，金沙兮粲彩。百界分身，面目儼在。闢一乘唱導之妙門，泯三觀互融之性海。其應物也清而有容，其行己也廉而匪介。豹澤霧以自文，鵬搏風而何快。不即不離，無對無待。

ClaimAnchors.Kwic: 合節，左右逢原，尊卑異位，開鑿人天正眼，󳭪張佛祖門庭，頭頭垂應物之機，著著有出身之路，如斯話會，猶落今時。且如何是不落今時底句？玲瓏八面自回合，峭峻一方誰敢窺？上堂，舉：密菴和尚示眾云：十五日已前，開池不待月；十五日已後，池成月自來；正當十五日，吹無孔笛、唱太平歌，佛及眾生齊聲唱和。且超群拔萃一句作麼生道？四海浪平龍睡穩，九天雲淨鶴飛高。師云：山僧今日因行，不妨掉臂。十五日已前，長在途中，不離家舍；十五日已後，長在家舍，不離途中；正當十五日，兩頭俱坐斷，一劒倚天寒。且超群拔萃一句作麼生道？擊拂子：一把柳絲收不得，和煙搭在玉欄干。退院，上堂。老向山中償宿債，拖犁拽耙十三年，如今筋骨條條露，鼻孔頑然不受穿。村草步，舊田園，桃花如錦柳如煙，放教臥月眠雲去，飢有青蒭渴有泉。拍禪牀，下座。真讚真讚門人師楷文斌汝均等編觀音觀音枯木巖前坐片時，輪珠數盡復思惟。南詢童子無消息，月在波心說向誰。魚籃觀音魚籃觀音籃裡魚，衣內珠。左提右挈，腥風滿途。茫茫宇宙人無數，那箇男兒是丈夫。達磨達磨聖諦廓然，忠言逆耳。折蘆渡江，事不獲已。脚下無風帀帀波，滔天沃日從茲始。寒山寒山天台山中，國清寺裡。掃󰆠隨身，塵埃滿地。只知指點笑他人，對面有人還笑你。拾得拾得爾名拾得，拾得者誰？不識一字，却要題詩。禿筆未曾輕點著，芭蕉葉上墨淋漓。維摩維摩嘆大褒圓，彈偏擊小。通身是病，自救不了。引得文殊問疾來，狼籍一場非小小。朝陽穿破衲朝陽穿破衲穴鼻針，無絲線。蹙斷雙眉，討頭未見。日炙風吹破衲衣，補得完全是幾時。對月了殘經對月了殘經看未了，歇不得，向下文長，付在來日。咄！者醃黑荳老僧，何曾解轉如是經？船子船子天無四壁地無門，舞棹呈橈誑後昆。索性和船都覆却，免教空記刻舟痕。永明壽禪師永明壽禪師道大德尊，宗通眼活，萬象森羅，熾然而說。游戲性海而一波不驚，披露覺天而十日竝出，實天台韶國師命世之寧馨，作兩浙錢大王福田之利益。至於秉五色筆，發佛祖潛光；鼓無絃琴，起衲僧痼疾。高風遠度，豐功偉蹟，豈片言隻字讚歎之所能及？咦！面目分明不覆藏，西湖水映中巖月。延慶秋墟入法師延慶秋墟入法師秋水兮澄神，金沙兮粲彩。百界分身，面目儼在。闢一乘唱導之妙門，泯三觀互融之性海。其應物也清而有容，其行己也廉而匪介。豹澤霧以自文，鵬搏風而何快。不即不離，無對無待。
ClaimAnchors.AttributionNote: Source record (X/X70/X70n1393.xml). Recorded sayings. Pingshi uses the pair in his own verse on Fish-Basket Guanyin, asking who can recognize the figure.
ClaimAnchors.ClaimText: 茫茫宇宙人無數，那箇男兒是丈夫

Senses.Explanation: Among countless people, who can answer as a person of resolve? Shaweng calls it a living phrase, and Gusu turns it on his gathered assembly. Hengshan asks it after a monk’s exchange; Pingshi places it in a Guanyin verse.
